records.title: Scalable reversible soliding: large-world acceleration, Rapier macro-dynamics and fracture
records.body:
## Owner priority and execution routing — 2026-10-27

**Approved owner intent, implementation Planned:** the first concrete #12
gameplay result is **an existing native-cell solid structure (tree) that,
after a real support/trunk cut, becomes a freely falling, toppling and
rolling Rapier rigid body.** A pre-authored/sleeping actor or manually
rotated tree cannot close this objective. Native material ownership,
static→dynamic collision fences, exact payload, valid refusal,
genuine angular motion and local structural cohesion/anchor admission
are required.

**Two independent tracks:**
- **Track A — dynamic structural detachment first:** [SOL-DETACH-001 #281](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/281)
  tracks the bounded *native-terrain-to-Rapier* proof and real tree
  acceptance. [Documentation PR #282](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/pull/282)
  contains the proposed canonical
  [structural-detachment charter](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/docs/sol-structural-detachment-primary-20261027/docs/operations/soliding-structural-detachment-programme.md)
  and a [2026-10-27 current-main/Noita reassessment](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/docs/sol-structural-detachment-primary-20261027/docs/audits/2026-10-27-issue12-stage3b-reassessment.md).
- **Track B — settled-region scaling/stationary acceleration:** retain
  current Stage-3B `#66 → #67 → #68 → #70` dependencies, #69's
  registered campaign, past #56–#65 evidence and separate parent
  Stage-4 admission. **#66 remains ready within Track B, not an
  automatic prerequisite for a finite event-driven Track-A tree proof.**
  Stage-4 performance, full Stage-6/7 fracture and persistence are
  not claimed complete.

**Current implementation boundary:** native World/Rapier already has
read-only settled-region observation and ordinary independent-body
coupling; it does **not** yet have an integrated arbitrary
native-solid detachment handoff. Reuse the existing asynchronous
desktop native-cell worker and main-thread Rapier owner. No default
material/liquid solver changes, full-world flood fill, duplicate
physics host, new cohesion for loose granular material or automatic
body-to-terrain welding. The optional Water-sheet idea is a separate
exploratory tangent, not this solid-tree milestone.

**Source/evidence note:** PR #282 is a **draft documentation change**
pending review and exact-head checks; it introduces no native
implementation or runtime pass. This addendum records the owner
priority immediately; the September 2026 checkpoint and original
stage ladder below are **preserved as dated historical programme
evidence and Track-B ordering**, not as the current universal
next-task instruction. No original validation receipt is superseded
outside an explicit new source-qualified review.

---

Parent: #8. Architecture context: #14/G-R and ADR-012. Prototype evidence: PR #23.

## Live Stage-3B checkpoint — 2026-09-20

Stage 3A remains the bounded reference/control; Stage 4 remains blocked. Stage-3B production authority is the #56-#70 chain and `docs/operations/soliding-stage3b-production-plan.md`.

At this checkpoint #56-#61 and #69 are complete. #61 landed through PR #89 as `db00e84e1b26b99f2816b6c1258d5dea97fc1fa1`. #62 is the next serialized central-World producer package; #63 follows it. #64 is the separable graph/index lane after #59/#60 and joins the producer lane at #65. #70 remains the exact-head campaign/parent-exit package.

The #79 remediation programme is parallel authority, **not a blanket #12 pause**. A remediation child touching the same World/body/test surfaces must inspect live ownership/write sets and stop on a real collision rather than duplicating work.

## Programme reclassification — 2026-09-19

**#12 remains OPEN and is now the foundational soliding programme, not merely the one-island prototype task.**

Owner intent is that reversible soliding is both a **major large-world performance mechanism** and a **gameplay-physics capability bridge**. Large settled or locally quiescent regions should be able to move through cheaper representations so CyberSand does not pay full fine-grained cellular cost everywhere in a large, high-activity world. When a coherent region becomes dynamic, handing its authoritative material payload to a Rapier aggregate also supplies macro-scale mechanics the cellular solver intentionally does not have: linear and angular momentum, inertia, torque, rotational motion, friction/contact response and body-level forces.

The accepted bounded work in PR #23 / ADR-012 is **Phase 0 evidence**. It proved important ownership and reversibility primitives, but it is not the terminal scope of #12 and merging/fixing PR #23 must not by itself close this issue.

This reclassification does not rewrite historical evidence. The 2026-09-13 result remains exactly what it was: an isolated, bounded prototype. It now serves as evidence and reusable implementation for the larger programme below.

## Core architecture question

Can CyberSand move settled regions through a **reversible representation lifecycle** that:

1. materially reduces CPU/work/memory/coupling cost in large active worlds; and
2. lets coherent material temporarily acquire useful macro-scale dynamics from Rapier — momentum, inertia, torque, rotation and rigid contact — then return safely to cellular or fragmented representations?

The performance and gameplay-physics purposes are co-equal. Dynamic Rapier aggregates are one upper tier of that lifecycle, not the definition of soliding itself.

A useful conceptual progression is:

```text
active cells
    |
    v
ordinary sleeping cells
    |
    v
tracked settled-region summary
    |
    v
stationary accelerated / proxy representation
    |
    +------> coherent dynamic Rapier aggregate
    |              |        |
    |              |        +--> impacts / torque / rotation / body forces
    |              |
    |              +--> fracture partition
    |                       |
    |                       +--> coherent child Rapier fragments
    |                       |
    |                       +--> local loose/settled cellular material
    |
    +<----- bounded local/full cellular reactivation <-----+
```

Not every material or region may enter every tier.

In particular, **"cheap to represent while quiescent" must never imply "rigidly cohesive."** Loose Sand may eventually qualify for summary/stationary acceleration while remaining ineligible for dynamic rigid-body promotion and immediately recovering avalanche behavior after invalidation.

## Two first-class purposes: acceleration and macro-dynamics

### Performance purpose

Large worlds should avoid repeatedly visiting, coupling and rebuilding every quiet interior cell when only a small boundary or distant region is active. Soliding should discover and maintain cheaper representations with measured amortized benefit, and decline promotion when churn makes the bookkeeping uneconomic.

### Gameplay-physics purpose

The cellular solver has no general conserved momentum, angular momentum, inertia tensor or torque state. It should not grow a universal per-cell velocity/rigid-body solver merely to make large coherent chunks tumble convincingly.

For admitted coherent regions, Rapier becomes the motion/contact owner while native soliding storage remains the authoritative material payload. During that dynamic interval Rapier may provide:

- linear velocity and momentum;
- angular velocity and angular momentum;
- mass, centre of mass and inertia derived from the admitted payload/shape;
- torque from off-centre contacts and forces;
- gravity, collision, friction, restitution and other explicitly admitted body mechanics;
- continuous transform/rotation of the aggregate without rasterizing it back into cells every tick.

Promotion does **not** need to manufacture missing historical cellular momentum. A near-rest region may enter Rapier with zero/known initial velocity and subsequently acquire motion through gravity, support loss, impacts or explicit forces. If a future path needs to preserve already-moving cellular momentum at promotion time, that requires a separately defined motion source/carrier rather than guessed velocity.

Reversibility exists so this richer body-scale physics is temporary rather than replacing CyberSand's material simulation.

## Phase 0 — accepted bounded prototype evidence

Retain the existing #12 / PR #23 result as the starting proof:

- bounded same-material candidate observation with face connectivity;
- no automatic cohesion for loose powders;
- exact stationary row/rectangle proxy geometry with cells retaining authority;
- prompt invalidation on relevant mutation/support changes;
- ADR-012 singular material ownership and fenced transitions;
- one-slot native payload with Rapier-owned transform/contact during aggregate motion;
- exact material/state/temperature restoration for admitted rectangles;
- revision/token/capacity/stale/cancel/failure/exclusion/quarantine handling;
- repeated 8x8 and 8x14 near-rest promotion/motion/quarter-turn/reversal;
- explicit refusal of unsupported arbitrary shapes, loose granular cohesion,
  energetic reversal, persistence and production asynchronous handoff.

Known prototype limitations remain real:

- discovery is a manually registered <=32x32 observer, not world-scale discovery;
- every maximum-size observation visits its witness area;
- dynamic admission is authored Wall/RedBrick rectangular material only;
- one native slot and one isolated manual main-thread coordinator;
- no production desktop-worker rendezvous or multi-region registry;
- no generalized split/merge/fracture;
- no aggregate save/import continuation;
- no proof that the prototype's observer/proxy path is itself a net large-world performance win;
- PR #23 is based on an older main and still has the recorded Linux/provenance integration blockers.

**Do not merge the old 79-file PR wholesale merely to make the issue look progressed.**
Port/rebase/reuse only the pieces that survive current-main review. Preserve the original branch and evidence as a recoverable control.

## Representation and eligibility model

Before broad implementation, maintain separate eligibility concepts.

### 1. Settled-summary eligibility

A region may be tracked/compacted for scheduling or discovery purposes when its relevant state is sufficiently stable. This says nothing about cohesion.

Inputs may include material/state, mutation age, activity, support/topology witnesses,
temperature/reaction state, transient-body occupancy, exclusion/region state and
pending events. Ordinary scheduler sleep alone is insufficient evidence.

### 2. Stationary-acceleration eligibility

A region may use a cheaper stationary representation only when current behavior can
be preserved through bounded boundary handling and prompt local invalidation.

Candidate implementations may include, and must be measured rather than assumed:

- cells retained as canonical payload plus coarse region skip/freeze metadata;
- exact/compact native region payload with derived boundary/collision data;
- merged rectangle/contour support proxies;
- hybrid interior compaction while retaining active boundary bands.

The programme must compare these alternatives. "Rapier collider exists" is not by
itself a performance architecture.

### 3. Dynamic-cohesive eligibility

A region may become a moving Rapier aggregate only when its material/state semantics
justify cohesion and the ownership handoff is admitted.

Loose granular rest is not cohesion. Supported Sand/Stone may become cheaper to
simulate while stationary without becoming a rigid projectile. Cohesion,
structural support and stationary acceleration are separate policy axes.

## Concurrency and programme boundaries

This work **may proceed in its own branch/worktree while #26 and #27 run**.

- #26 keeps its exact source-matched Water baseline/candidates. #12 must not mutate
  or reinterpret that experiment's control.
- #27/MS-000 may continue its common scenario apparatus independently. Soliding may
  later consume MicroScenario fixtures, but does not wait for #27 to begin architecture,
  discovery or performance work.
- #18/#20 are not prerequisites for stationary acceleration or the existing
  near-rest aggregate proof. Energetic demotion, moving fragments or a later
  high-speed carrier may depend on their results or a separately admitted mechanism.
- #29/intermaterial rules remain authoritative for reactions/state changes.
  Soliding must wake/demote affected regions rather than duplicating interaction
  semantics inside the representation layer.
- #14/G-final may consume relevant soliding evidence but **full completion of this
  performance programme is not retroactively made a blanket G-final dependency.**
- Existing ADR ownership, failed-world, immutable handoff, region/exclusion,
  capacity and deterministic-ordering contracts remain in force unless explicitly
  revised by a reviewed ADR.

Branch isolation protects implementation concurrency; **source identity protects
experimental validity**. Do not merge an experimental soliding branch into another
active experiment merely for convenience.

## Stage 1 — current-main reconciliation and reusable kernel

Goal: turn Phase 0 into a trustworthy starting substrate without confusing old
prototype integration with programme completion.

1. Review PR #23 against current main and current #11/#19/#26-era contracts.
2. Classify each #23 change as:
   - reusable unchanged;
   - reusable after current-main adaptation;
   - historical evidence/test only;
   - obsolete/conflicting and not to port.
3. Preserve ADR-012 and the dated audit as historical Phase 0 evidence.
4. Reproduce the essential owner/state/conservation transition tests on a
   current-main-compatible branch before extending semantics.
5. Resolve the GLIBC/runtime-provenance blockers if the reusable implementation is
   to be integrated; do not weaken the <=2.34 runtime floor or artifact identity gates.
6. Keep the initial implementation opt-in until the later performance and behavior
   gates justify ordinary runtime use.

**Exit:** current-main-compatible reusable soliding primitives exist, or the retained
Phase 0 branch is explicitly kept as the control while successor code replaces it.
No old evidence is rewritten.

## Stage 2 — representation state machine and scalable region identity

Goal: define the production-scale lifecycle before introducing world-wide discovery.

Specify and test:

- stable region/aggregate IDs plus nonwrapping or explicitly refusing generations;
- representation states and sole owner in every state;
- exact payload/state/temperature ownership;
- boundary/interface meaning for neighboring active cells;
- entry/exit prerequisites and hysteresis;
- local invalidation and wake reasons;
- event, reaction, heat, body-contact, support/topology and edit interactions;
- region split/merge identity rules;
- capacity/full-queue outcomes;
- deterministic transition ordering;
- exclusion/re-entry semantics;
- failed-world/quarantine behavior;
- snapshot/render/collision visibility during transitions;
- persistence boundary and what is explicitly not serializable yet.

A refusal to promote or compact must always leave the old representation valid.
There must be no state in which material is missing, owned twice, or silently
discarded.

**Exit:** reviewed lifecycle/state table and focused transition tests precede
world-scale optimization code.

## Stage 3 — incremental world-scale discovery and tracking

Goal: replace the <=32x32 observer with bounded discovery whose cost scales with
**change**, not total world area.

Prefer existing dirty/activity/chunk metadata and incremental summaries over periodic
global flood-fills.

Required properties:

- work originates from changed/dirty regions or bounded maintenance queues;
- components may continue across chunk/block boundaries without one-tick global walks;
- face connectivity, holes, seams and material/state boundaries remain explicit;
- local region revisions invalidate stale work;
- fixed/bounded queues and scratch capacities have explicit defer/refuse outcomes;
- overloaded discovery may lag safely; it may not partially publish a candidate;
- deterministic ordering is retained across worker counts where Current contracts
  require it;
- offscreen exclusion does not manufacture rest;
- change-and-restore / ABA-sensitive state has an adequate mutation witness;
- instrumentation-off or feature-disabled behavior is authoritative-baseline neutral.

Measure at minimum:

- cells/blocks/chunks inspected for discovery;
- dirty-to-reclassified latency;
- candidate churn and false invalidations;
- region count/area distribution;
- queue/scratch high-water and refusals;
- CPU time and memory per tracked area;
- wake/rebuild amplification after localized edits.

**Exit:** discovery can cover large worlds without an unbounded scan and has a measured
amortized cost model. Do not proceed by choosing a region-size threshold by intuition.

## Stage 4 — stationary acceleration bake-off

Goal: obtain useful performance **before** requiring widespread dynamic aggregation.

Compare at least the relevant feasible candidates against ordinary Current sleep:

A. baseline cells + existing scheduler sleep;
B. cells retained + settled-region summary/skip metadata;
C. stationary derived collision/support proxy;
D. compact/frozen stationary payload or boundary-band representation, if justified
   by the earlier measurements.

Controlled tests must determine whether each candidate actually saves work. A new
region manager that merely adds bookkeeping to already-sleeping cells is a failed
optimization, not progress.

Required behavior:

- adjacent active liquids/powders/reactions see valid boundaries;
- local excavation/edit invalidates only the required area/halo where possible;
- support removal can reactivate granular material promptly;
- nearby activity does not force needless full-region cellular work;
- player/body collision has one support/contact owner;
- renderer receives truthful material state without requiring the full simulation
  representation to stay active;
- no scenario-specific physics is added to maintain the illusion.

Derive measured **break-even curves** for region area, quiet duration, boundary
activity and churn. Promotion/compaction thresholds should follow those curves.

**Exit:** at least one stationary tier demonstrates a reproducible net saving on
representative large-world workloads without changing protected material behavior,
or the programme records that this tier is not worthwhile and proceeds with the
evidence.

## Stage 5 — granular and solid eligibility semantics

Goal: capture the performance benefit for Sand/Stone/other large settled regions
without accidental cementing.

Build an explicit material/state eligibility policy distinguishing at least:

- permanently/intrinsically cohesive construction solids;
- loose granular material;
- supported/packed granular material;
- braced or stateful variants such as applicable Stone modes;
- reactive/hot/phase-changing regions;
- mixed-material boundaries.

For granular material, determine what evidence permits:

- summary/skip acceleration;
- stationary support/collision proxying;
- interior compaction;
- **not** dynamic rigid cohesion.

Loss of support, erosion, excavation, reactions, body impact or material-specific
state changes must recover the appropriate cellular behavior. Qualification should
be conservative; false negatives cost performance, while false positives can change
gameplay physics.

Do not invent a universal structural-integrity simulation merely to authorize
soliding. If dynamic granular cohesion later requires one, admit it separately.

**Exit:** large Sand/Stone fixtures can enter useful cheap stationary tiers and
recover avalanche/support behavior under controlled disturbances, while loose-pile
controls never become rigid merely because they rested.

## Stage 6 — production multi-region ownership and dynamic-physics handoff

Goal: generalize ADR-012's one-slot manual proof into bounded real runtime operation
for materials that genuinely qualify for dynamic aggregation, with Rapier deliberately
supplying the macro momentum/inertia/torque/contact mechanics that the cellular
representation lacks.

Required design:

- fixed or bounded aggregate registry with stable generation-bearing handles;
- bounded worker<->main-thread request/ack/result queues;
- native workers never access live Godot/Rapier objects;
- main thread alone creates/mutates Rapier RIDs;
- revision-checked prepare / acknowledge / commit / topology-finalize protocol;
- preflight membership/payload/shape/body/result/destination capacity;
- exact sole material owner at every phase;
- stale/cancel/full-capacity paths retain the current representation;
- no collision hole or stale self-collider during handoff;
- deterministic transition ordering where multiple candidates compete;
- bounded re-entry/exclusion behavior;
- quarantine rather than invented rollback after an unexpected postcommit failure;
- explicit mass, centre-of-mass and inertia derivation from authoritative membership;
- declared mapping between CyberSand cell/pixel units and Rapier motion/force units;
- initial velocity/angular-velocity policy: near-rest zero/known input unless a real
  source of prior motion has been admitted;
- body-level gravity/contact/friction/torque behavior without per-tick erase/rasterize/restore;
- immutable/copy motion observations crossing back to native code when fracture,
  demotion or diagnostics require them;
- no requirement that ordinary cells acquire persistent vx/vy merely because an
  aggregate can move.

Measure registry contention, bridge traffic, transition latency, shape creation cost,
main-thread budget and Rapier body/contact cost as well as native tick cost. Record
linear/angular motion, contact impulses/torques and energy changes with declared units;
do not imply exact continuum conservation from Rapier/cellular coupling.

**Exit:** multiple aggregates can promote, accelerate, collide, translate, rotate and
reverse/fracture under real desktop asynchronous ownership and supported Web sequencing,
with useful momentum/inertia/torque behavior, exact admitted payload accounting and
bounded failure behavior.

## Stage 7 — geometry hierarchy, fracture and controlled return to pixels

Goal: make reversibility physically useful. A damaged/moving aggregate must not
collapse into the pathological result where **the whole coherent body suddenly turns
into a loose pixel cloud** merely because one part fractured or became invalid.

Use a measured geometry ladder, for example:

1. exact rectangles;
2. merged rectangles / orthogonal runs;
3. bounded contour or convex/decomposition representation where it clearly pays;
4. more complex forms only with evidence.

For every tier measure shape count, build/update cost, contact fidelity, holes,
thin necks, concavity error and Rapier cost. Refuse over-complex promotion rather
than silently simplifying important topology.

### Fracture is a core representation transition

Fracture should partition the authoritative aggregate membership into bounded,
material-meaningful components after damage, impact, support loss, excavation,
reaction/thermal weakening or other admitted fracture triggers.

Each resulting component is classified independently:

- **coherent dynamic fragment:** remains/creates a child Rapier aggregate;
- **coherent stationary fragment:** may enter a stationary accelerated tier;
- **loose cellular fragment/debris:** returns only the affected cells to the
  cellular solver;
- **unrepresentable/capacity-limited result:** retain the prior safe owner or
  defer the fracture rather than deleting material or emitting an uncontrolled cloud.

Large unaffected portions should remain aggregated. One chipped corner should not
force a thousand-cell slab to dissolve wholesale.

### Motion inheritance across fracture

When one moving Rapier aggregate splits into coherent child aggregates, initialize
each child from the parent's sampled rigid-body state rather than discarding motion.

At minimum evaluate:

- child centre-of-mass linear velocity from parent translation plus rotational
  point velocity at the child COM;
- inherited angular velocity where physically appropriate;
- child mass and inertia recomputed from its membership/shape;
- optional bounded fracture impulses with an explicit source and zero-net or
  otherwise accounted momentum policy;
- total linear/angular momentum and kinetic-energy error before/after the split;
- contact separation so new children do not begin with pathological self-overlap.

Exact physical conservation may be limited by raster geometry, contact state and
the deliberately approximate CyberSand/Rapier coupling, but errors must be measured
and bounded rather than silently resetting every fragment to rest.

This mechanism is deliberately preferable to adding persistent velocity to every
pixel. Significant moving chunks can stay in the representation that actually has
momentum/torque; material only returns to ordinary cells where cellular behavior
is the useful representation.

### Local cellular reactivation

Reactivation should be spatially bounded:

- split out the disturbed subregion plus required halo;
- retain unaffected settled/solided regions where safe;
- support excavation, local melting/heating, reaction fronts and structural loss;
- prevent one changed cell from gratuitously waking a huge world-scale aggregate;
- preserve identity and exact payload accounting across split/merge/refusal;
- when loose pixels are emitted from a moving body, explicitly document how much
  body motion is discarded, converted into another admitted carrier, or retained
  by surrounding child aggregates.

#20-style sparse high-speed carriers may complement this for tiny energetic debris,
but **fracturing coherent #12 aggregates is not conditional on #20 existing**.

**Exit:** impacts/damage can turn one aggregate into a bounded set of coherent moving
fragments plus only the genuinely loose/reactivated cellular material; useful
macro momentum/rotation is retained rather than globally zeroed, and local edits do
not cause catastrophic whole-region wake/rebuild cost.

## Stage 8 — persistence, streaming and long-lived representation truthfulness

Before claiming production continuation for solided worlds:

- version region/aggregate schema and representation policy;
- persist the sole authoritative payload, identity/generation and required state;
- define pending-transition save refusal or safe drain semantics;
- define load validation and refusal;
- record source/config/profile identities needed for truthful replay claims;
- reconcile interest-region/streaming behavior without earning fake rest;
- never serialize compiler struct bytes or omit aggregate-owned material.

Exact replay is not implied merely by save/load support. Until this stage is
completed, saves taken during unsupported aggregate states must explicitly refuse or
drain to a supported representation.

## Stage 9 — large-world performance and behavior campaign

This stage decides whether the architecture fulfills its reason for existing.

Run source-matched A/B campaigns using representative desktop hardware, including
the owner-designated Ryzen 2600X development machine where available. CI/private
runners remain valuable for correctness, determinism and broad sweeps; uncontended
local runs are preferred for desktop performance comparisons.

Workloads should include at least:

- huge mostly-settled construction/terrain with localized active work;
- large granular bed with excavation and support loss;
- sustained Water/material activity beside large stable terrain;
- repeated local impacts/explosions causing bounded wake regions;
- mixed active "chaos" world with large quiet interiors;
- coherent dynamic aggregate translation/rotation under off-centre impacts;
- falling/support-loss slabs that acquire Rapier momentum and torque;
- fracture of a moving coherent body into several child fragments plus local debris;
- repeated fracture -> settle -> re-solidify cycles;
- churn-heavy negative control where soliding should decline or quickly demote.

Use MicroScenarios when the common host is stable enough, but do not make #27 a
prerequisite for equivalent deterministic fixtures.

Compare the relevant representation tiers separately. Measure at minimum:

- simulation/tick p50/p95/p99/max and total run cost;
- frame/main-thread cost where Rapier/proxy work matters;
- visited cells, active blocks/chunks and scheduled cores;
- discovery/maintenance/wake/rebuild work;
- aggregate/proxy counts and geometry complexity;
- native and bridge memory;
- queue/capacity high-water/refusal;
- Rapier shape/body/contact work;
- linear/angular momentum, torque response and rotation where dynamic tiers are active;
- fracture partition/build cost and fragment-count high-water;
- momentum/angular-momentum/energy error across admitted fracture transitions;
- promotion/demotion/fracture amortization;
- wake amplification from local edits;
- time/area/churn break-even points;
- deterministic/repeat/worker parity where required;
- conservation/state/temperature/source-sink invariants.

Do not preregister a fake universal percentage improvement before measuring Current.
The acceptance question is whether the system provides **material net savings in
the large settled/high-activity worlds it exists to enable**, while declining
cleanly when churn makes soliding uneconomic.

A negative result for a specific tier is valid evidence; remove or narrow that tier
rather than hiding its overhead behind a larger test.

## Programme-level acceptance

#12 is not complete merely because PR #23 merges.

The programme reaches its completion gate when all of the following have either a
passing implementation or an explicit evidence-backed no-go/defer disposition:

- [ ] Phase 0 evidence is preserved and current-main successor/reuse is reconciled.
- [ ] Representation states, owners, IDs/generations and failure transitions are explicit.
- [ ] World-scale discovery is incremental/bounded rather than periodic full-world scanning.
- [ ] Ordinary existing sleep is measured as the control; soliding overhead is not assumed free.
- [ ] At least one stationary acceleration tier has a measured break-even and useful large-world result, or is explicitly rejected.
- [ ] Granular acceleration does not create false cohesion and recovers collapse/support behavior after invalidation.
- [ ] Local edits/reactions/heat/support changes produce bounded local wake/reclassification.
- [ ] Dynamic coherent aggregates, if retained, use bounded production ownership handoff with no missing/double material or collision ownership.
- [ ] Dynamic aggregate gameplay demonstrates useful Rapier-provided translation, rotation, inertia and torque without requiring a universal cellular velocity field.
- [ ] Fracture can preserve coherent child fragments and bounded inherited macro motion instead of forcing whole-body pixel-cloud demotion.
- [ ] Geometry and fracture complexity/capacity/refusal behavior is explicit.
- [ ] Exact admitted payload/state/temperature accounting survives repeated transitions.
- [ ] Exclusion/re-entry, failed-world, cancellation, stale generations and saturation have retained tests.
- [ ] Persistence is either implemented truthfully or unsupported representation states explicitly refuse/drain saves.
- [ ] Large-world A/B evidence records source/artifact/hardware/config identities and demonstrates where the architecture wins and loses.
- [ ] Current ownership/coupling/soliding documentation, ADRs, roadmap, retrieval routes and issue mirrors are synchronized.
- [ ] Historical failures, rejected candidates and PR #23 evidence remain retained.

If implementation size becomes unsuitable for a single issue, create bounded child
issues for the stages above while keeping #12 as the canonical programme tracker.
Do not recreate a fake serial order from issue numbers.

## Immediate next action — 2026-09-20

Continue from authoritative current main with #62 as the next central-World producer package. #64 may proceed in parallel only while its actual write set remains disjoint from #62/#63. Join at #65, then #66 -> #67 -> #68; execute #70 only after #68 and the already-complete #69 preregistration are reconciled to one frozen exact-head candidate.

Do not self-admit Stage 3B. Stage 4, stationary acceleration, cohesion, Rapier ownership transfer and fracture remain blocked until the Stage-3B parent decision.

records.title: Architecture experiment: measure liquid state precision at fixed layout and semantics
records.body:
## Completed P1 / P2 / P3 — 2026-09-11

**#17/P is complete.** [G-P is recorded in #14](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/14#issuecomment-5633025806). [Complete evidence, precision/threshold/delay tables and validation](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/5fdca7c/docs/audits/2026-09-11-issue-17-state-precision.md) are published on the separate `codex/issue-17-state-precision` branch.

**Retain mass8 as the reference; Water-only delay4 exactly preserves 0..12 semantics.** All1,328 behavior processes conserve exact per-arm integer quantity. Worker/repeat/delay comparisons and simultaneous-worker tests pass. All392 timing processes and36 extended controls are retained. Coarse arms preserve films but lose levelness/discharge and tiny initial inputs. Mass10 provides modest improvement with extra narrow/ledge work; P2 threshold effects remain separate.

Source **f3fb9de**, registration **6ae3dd5**, implementation **8fff609**, concurrency/reducer **af17fcc**, completed evidence **5fdca7c**. One fixed carrier (8/8/8 size/stride/alignment), epoch8, unchanged Water algorithm and scheduler geometry. No production merge/migration; original DLL remains untouched.

G-P selects at most a downstream experimental state budget, not production Cell layout or Water precision. #18's precision prerequisite is satisfied but its concrete motion-target admission remains required; #19 independent; #20 blocked; #14/G-final open. Host/platform, shared-desktop timing and inherited provenance failures remain explicit in the report.

The original scope and execution prompt below are retained as the task's acceptance contract.

Programme / staged decision record: #14. Workstream: P.

## Purpose

Quantify what mass and auxiliary precision buy, independently from Cell width and solver/motion changes.

## Architecture question

Which of4/6/8/10 mass bits and a separately packed coherent-delay field preserve useful liquid behavior and at what total-work cost?

## Dependencies

records.title: Architecture experiment: fractional liquid presentation and Water Feel Lab
records.body:
## Revised scope — 2026-09-11

This issue is expanded before implementation to combine the original **fractional-liquid presentation experiment** with the **engineering/preparation stage for later human-led Water feel evaluation**.

The issue still does **not** choose a preferred Water precision, coherent-delay duration, production Cell packing, or gameplay default. Its new second responsibility is to leave behind a verified, reproducible **Water Feel Lab** in which those semantic choices can be selected immediately before a run, without recompilation, and judged later under a fixed and understood presentation path.

Completed #17 remains the quantitative precision reference. Its result is not reversed: **mass8 remains the numerical reference/oracle and Water delay 0..12 is exactly representable in four bits.** However, numerical divergence from mass8 is not by itself a gameplay rejection criterion. #17 established what changes quantitatively; this issue establishes how Water is presented and constructs a trustworthy apparatus for later perceptual evaluation.

Programme / staged decision record: #14. Workstream: V, expanded with H-preparation. Human preference/acceptance remains a later gate.

## Purpose

1. Complete the original presentation experiment: determine whether four-level fractional coverage plus local interface reconstruction improves visible Water surfaces, droplets and boundaries without changing authoritative simulation state.
2. Extend the existing #13 Experiment Tower into a broad deterministic **Water Feel Lab**.
3. Replace compile-time-only precision experimentation with a validated **runtime Water semantic policy** suitable for human A/B and blinded testing, while keeping the physical storage carrier deliberately wider than any candidate semantic budget.
4. Verify that known #17 configurations reproduce their registered semantics in the runtime harness before adding previously untested 3/5/7-bit mass and altered coherent-duration candidates.
5. Finish with a trusted test environment and candidate-generation mechanism. **Do not select a perceptual winner in this issue.**

## Architecture questions

### V — presentation

Can a fixed, compact **four visible partial-fill level** presentation, optionally assisted by local 3x3 interface reconstruction, make fractional Water readable and attractive across top surfaces, undersides, side boundaries, diagonals, droplets and thin streams without mutating authoritative mass?

### H-preparation — experimental semantics

Can Water quantity precision and coherent duration be parameterized at **World creation time** so that arbitrary registered human-test configurations can be selected through one common policy interface, without builds/recompilation and without unsafe mid-tick mutation?

Can this be done while preserving exact per-configuration integer conservation, deterministic repeat/worker behavior, current ownership/failure/region contracts, and enough correspondence with #17 to trust later human judgments?

## Dependencies and current evidence

- #15/G-C is complete and supplies stable presentation/behavior context.
- #16/G-L is complete and supplies experimental carrier/packing evidence. It does not select production width.
- #17/G-P is complete and supplies the numerical precision oracle, registered quantization rules, known 4/6/8/10-bit behavior, threshold separation and exact delay4 representation of existing 0..12 semantics.
- #13 is closed but its five-floor Experiment Tower, deterministic recipes, profile/reset concepts and human-facing testing intent are reusable infrastructure and should be extended rather than duplicated.
- #18 remains held for a concrete directional-persistence target. The later human evaluation enabled by this issue may supply such a target, or may support a no-go.
- #20 remains blocked by #18/G-M and is unchanged by this issue.

This issue does not require a production layout decision. Optional history-assisted presentation remains a later stage only if #18 independently justifies useful history.

## Core decision principle

**Quantitative equivalence and perceptual adequacy are separate gates.**

For Water candidates:

- correctness/invariants determine whether a candidate is safe enough to observe;
- quantitative diagnostics describe how its behavior differs;
- later controlled human evaluation determines whether those differences are desirable, acceptable or objectionable for the game.

A candidate is not rejected in this issue merely because its basin residual, discharge, settling time or tiny-quantity behavior differs from mass8. Conversely, subjective preference can never waive material loss/duplication, broken ownership, nondeterministic policy application, unbounded work or invalid failure/region behavior.

## Scope

### Stage V1 — fractional presentation

Retain the original presentation scope, but make the intended human-test rendering explicit:

- current display path as reference;
- **four visible Water partial-fill levels** as the primary experimental presentation budget;
- local 3x3 mass-gradient/interface reconstruction for orientation where useful;
- deterministic gravity-oriented fallback for settled/weak-gradient surfaces;
- centered-droplet fallback for isolated/ambiguous tiny regions where appropriate;
- top, underside, vertical, diagonal and concave boundaries;
- adjacent-cell continuity and temporal stability;
- 1x and representative enlarged display scales;
- no authoritative mass mutation for visual smoothing.

Presentation modes may be hot-switched live where they affect rendering only. Hold authoritative simulation fixed for direct presentation comparisons.

### Stage V2 — Water Feel Lab infrastructure

Extend/reuse the #13 Experiment Tower rather than building an unrelated benchmark application. Add a dedicated Water Feel Lab floor/annex or equivalent clearly selectable area with deterministic recipes and one-action reset.

The lab must support repeatable scenarios spanning at least:

| Scenario family | Required cases / intent |
|---|---|
| Flat pooling | broad shallow basin, deep basin, wide calm settling, connected pools at different starting heights |
| Small quantities | isolated partial cells, repeated tiny drips accumulating into visible Water, low-flow trickle, residual pockets |
| Channels / geometry | narrow and broad channels, stair/step terrain, U-shaped vessel, constriction/nozzle, irregular/sloped bed |
| Releases | fast reservoir dump, slow gate opening, vertical fall, ledge sheet, thin stream, shower/drizzle |
| Directional motion | vertical jet and horizontal/diagonal emission reference suitable for later #18 admission discussion |
| Terrain interaction | excavation then refill, support removal, cavity filling/draining, real voids and barriers |
| Material interaction | Water over/through Sand using preserved #13 baseline policy, downstream deposition/settling observations, protected Mercury reference kept separate |
| Player/body interaction | player disturbance where supported; representative rigid-body displacement only if the existing source-matched path is already available and does not broaden scope |
| Films / boundaries | supported film, underside/side interface, droplets crossing storage/activity/core seams |
| Long-tail feel | settling, lingering micro-motion, apparent stickiness/crawling, abrupt stopping and repeat reset |

Use the intended four-level presentation for semantic human-test comparisons unless the tester explicitly selects a presentation study. The lab must make it difficult to accidentally compare both simulation precision and render precision at the same time.

## Runtime Water semantic policy

Implement one validated immutable-at-runtime policy structure consumed when constructing/restarting an experiment World. Exact names may follow repository conventions, but conceptually it contains:

```text
WaterExperimentPolicy
  mass_bits                integer 3..8
  coherence_ticks          integer 0..12
  rest_policy              registered enum/policy, default current-normalized behavior
  render_fill_levels       default 4; presentation-only
  interface_mode           presentation-only
  scenario_id
  seed / deterministic recipe identity
```

The policy may include derived values such as `mass_max`, quantized film threshold and rest tolerance. Compute those once at configuration/application time; do not perform avoidable powers/scaling setup inside the hot loop.

### Required mass range

Support every integer width **3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8** for Water human-test semantics.

These are semantic precision settings inside a superset experimental storage representation. They are **not six different production Cell layouts** and do not imply bitstream packing across cell boundaries.

The runtime path must use the same registered nearest/half-up physical quantization rule as #17 unless a separately named policy is intentionally selected and identified. Preserve the exact integer ledger within each candidate lattice; initial quantization error remains separate from runtime drift.

### Required coherent-duration range

Allow `coherence_ticks` to be selected at runtime from **0..12**, with named convenience candidates including:

- 12 — current behavior/reference;
- 7 — maximum duration that would fit a 3-bit semantic field;
- 3 — aggressive shorter-coherence candidate / 2-bit maximum;
- 0 — no-coherence behavioral reference.

Do not confuse duration with physical storage width. Existing 0..12 semantics still require four bits if preserved exactly; shortening the maximum countdown deliberately changes behavior and is therefore a human-test candidate, not a lossless packing result.

### Runtime selection surfaces

Expose the **same normalized policy** through all of:

1. an in-game developer popup/panel;
2. a versioned profile/config file;
3. launch/command-line arguments or the closest existing launch-configuration mechanism.

Do not implement three independent configuration systems. All three must resolve into one validated effective policy with the effective values/provenance visible in the UI or exported observation metadata.

Example intent only:

```text
--water-mass-bits=5
--water-coherence=7
--water-render-levels=4
--water-interface=oriented
--experiment=shallow-pool
--seed=18472
```

Profiles should be saveable/loadable separately from world/save-state compatibility unless the existing profile infrastructure already provides a safe versioned place.

## Apply/reset semantics

Simulation-semantic policy must **not** be mutated underneath active workers.

Preferred user flow:

1. pause or open Water Feel Lab panel;
2. select/edit policy;
3. validate the complete policy;
4. **Apply + Reset Experiment** at the existing exclusive owner boundary;
5. construct/reset a fresh deterministic World/recipe using that policy;
6. run, pause, single-step or restart the exact scenario.

A failed/invalid policy must leave the current running World/configuration intact.

Render-only settings may switch immediately where safe because they do not alter authoritative simulation state.

Do not make arbitrary mid-run mass-lattice conversion the normal A/B mechanism. Converting existing cells from, for example, 173/255 into a 4-bit lattice injects a new quantization event and confounds the comparison. Such live conversion may be tested separately for robustness but is not the controlled human-testing path.

## Blind and A/B testing support

Prepare—not perform—the later human test.

Support anonymous candidate labels such as A/B/C rather than exposing bit counts by default. A blind set maps labels to complete Water policies and records the hidden mapping in exported metadata.

Required workflow:

- choose scenario and deterministic seed/recipe;
- choose or randomize a candidate set;
- run candidate A;
- one action resets the identical scenario under candidate B/C/etc.;
- preserve camera/player starting state and scheduled release sequence where applicable;
- optional reveal only after observations are recorded;
- export enough metadata to reconstruct the tested configurations exactly.

Do not collect or interpret a final preferred state budget as part of #19 acceptance. The later H gate owns that decision.

## Ground-truth / trust requirements against #17

The runtime harness must earn trust before new human-test candidates are relied upon.

At minimum:

- mass8 runtime reference reproduces current/source-authoritative behavior in the relevant shared fixtures;
- runtime mass4, mass6 and mass8 reproduce #17 semantic/ledger expectations for shared fixtures within the intended comparison scope;
- mass10 need not become a general runtime Feel Lab candidate if the production-facing policy intentionally caps human testing at8 bits, but #17 remains the external higher-precision numerical reference;
- current coherence12 behavior reproduces the source reference;
- storage of current coherence semantics in a wider runtime lane does not change behavior;
- the policy path preserves the #17 distinction between initial quantization and runtime drift;
- worker1/4 and repeat comparisons are exact where the current native contract expects parity;
- observer/debug/UI state does not silently change simulation semantics;
- runtime policy identity is recorded with every deterministic test run.

New mass3/5/7 and shortened-coherence candidates are characterized enough to catch arithmetic errors and gross invalidity, but this issue does not require a #17-scale full timing campaign for every candidate.

## Controlled variables

### Presentation comparisons

Change presentation only. Authoritative material/mass/activity/collision/epoch/input remain identical.

### Semantic Feel Lab comparisons

Change only the selected Water policy fields for the registered candidate. Hold:

- scenario recipe and seed;
- renderer/four-level presentation;
- viewport/camera/start position;
- release schedule/input sequence;
- geometry/scheduler/worker configuration;
- #10/#13 material interaction policy;
- unrelated material state;
- ownership/failure/region contracts.

A combined mass+coherence candidate is allowed only after the interface supports isolated settings cleanly; #19 need not rank combinations.

## Instrumentation and observation metadata

Retain the useful quantitative context without turning the Feel Lab into another full scientific campaign.

For reproducible runs expose/export as appropriate:

- effective Water policy and profile/version/hash;
- scenario/seed/release schedule;
- source/artifact/platform/worker identity;
- exact per-run integer Water quantity and any explicit source/sink/outflow accounting;
- initial physical quantization error;
- optional visits/transfers/active blocks/last-change/rest summary;
- presentation mode/fill levels;
- screenshots/video capture hooks if already available;
- anonymous candidate label plus hidden mapping for blind tests.

Quantitative outputs are descriptive context for later human judgment, not an automatic ranking function.

## Presentation instrumentation

Retain the original V measurements:

- rendered coverage error versus normalized mass on synthetic/frozen frames;
- orientation/boundary discontinuity failures;
- temporal flicker on fixed sequences;
- CPU snapshot/copy cost and bytes/high-water;
- actual upload size and render/GPU timing where measurable;
- authoritative content/hash/activity equality across presentation modes;
- immutable delayed-consumer handoff regressions.

Do not infer a GPU or bandwidth saving without measuring the actual path.

## Non-goals

- No production Water precision migration.
- No production Cell-layout selection or repacking.
- No bitstream packing across cell boundaries.
- No claim that mass8 is perceptually optimal or that lower precision is perceptually acceptable.
- No final human preference/acceptance study or owner sign-off.
- No universal velocity field, compact flow history, pressure/Navier-Stokes solver or #18 implementation.
- No sparse ballistic system or #20 implementation.
- No generalized liquid unification or reaction retuning.
- No relaxation of exact per-candidate closed integer conservation.
- No full-Cell GPU upload merely to expose experimental settings.
- No authoritative render orientation.
- No connected-component centroid system or unrelated body renderer.
- No unsafe mutation of simulation policy while workers are executing.

## Preservation requirements

Preserve protected current behavior except where the registered Water candidate deliberately changes the tested semantic variable. Keep Mercury/powder references and #13 Baseline policy distinct. Preserve state/temperature transfer, bounded work, immutable handoff, failed-world quarantine and region pause/re-entry contracts. Retain original control binaries/fixtures; fresh-world comparisons never reinterpret old save bytes as a new layout.

No universal flow field or new representation is implied by freed candidate bits. Reclaimable semantic capacity is evidence for later packing/motion decisions, not permission to spend it in this issue.

## Validation

### Native semantic validation

- focused Water quantity/conservation tests for every supported runtime mass width;
- legal policy/range validation and refusal tests;
- repeat and matching worker-count semantic checks;
- current mass8/current-coherence source reference comparison;
- shared #17 fixture reproduction for mass4/6/8 sufficient to establish harness correspondence;
- mass3/5/7 arithmetic boundary and low-quantity tests;
- coherence0..12 countdown/reset/merge validation as applicable;
- invalid Apply must not replace the running World;
- profile/config/CLI/UI resolution must produce the same effective policy.

### Presentation/application validation

- actual native desktop walkthrough of all lab scenarios;
- real Web compatibility/threaded presentation/runtime-policy path if those targets expose the lab;
- panel navigation, Apply+Reset, pause/single-step, deterministic reset, candidate switch and blind labels;
- no accidental chemistry/material contamination between test bays;
- labels/scenario purpose readable without polluting ordinary gameplay UI;
- delayed render consumer/immutable snapshot regressions.

Record unavailable platform targets rather than inferring acceptance.

### Documentation / repository validation

Synchronize the revised programme/prompt/status documentation, material appearance/Water contracts, Experiment Tower documentation, controls, roadmap and retrieval routes. Preserve historical M11 hashes and disclose inherited publication/provenance failures rather than rewriting them. Run the repository's required docs/history/retrieval/diff checks.

## Acceptance criteria

#19 is complete only when both V1 and V2 are satisfied or an explicit evidence-backed no-go is recorded for a substage.

### V1 — presentation

- Four-level partial-fill presentation is implemented as a selectable, documented experimental mode.
- Orientation/fallback behavior is demonstrated across top/under/side/diagonal/ambiguous cases with retained positive and negative visuals.
- Same authoritative input remains unchanged across presentation modes.
- Coverage/artifact/cost evidence and immutable-handoff checks are retained.
- No production render migration is silently selected.

### V2 — Water Feel Lab

- Existing #13 Experiment Tower is extended/reused with the broad Water scenario suite above.
- Runtime Water mass precision 3..8 is selectable without recompilation.
- Runtime coherent duration 0..12 is selectable without recompilation, with named 12/7/3/0 candidates.
- In-game panel, versioned profile/config and launch arguments resolve to one effective policy.
- Simulation-semantic changes use validated Apply+Reset/fresh-world semantics; render-only controls can switch live where safe.
- Known mass4/6/8 and current coherence behavior correspond with #17/current controls strongly enough to establish harness trust.
- Exact per-candidate integer conservation and deterministic worker/repeat requirements pass.
- Blind A/B candidate labels and deterministic same-scenario reset are functional.
- Runtime policy/scenario/source identity can be exported/reconstructed.
- The suite has been manually walked through to verify that every scenario actually functions as intended.
- **No candidate is declared perceptually superior, acceptable or production-ready by #19.**

A sound negative result remains successful completion when supported by retained evidence. Do not optimize candidates after seeing human-preference outcomes because those outcomes are not collected here.

## Required evidence artefacts

- Revised experiment registration and runtime-policy contract.
- Source/build/platform identities.
- Frozen presentation frames and screenshot/video comparisons.
- Coverage/artifact/cost table.
- Runtime-policy validation matrix for mass3..8 and coherence0..12.
- #17 correspondence/reproduction table for shared reference variants.
- Experiment Tower / Water Feel Lab scenario manifest and deterministic recipes.
- UI/config/CLI equivalence tests and example profiles.
- Blind-candidate metadata/replay demonstration.
- Conservation/repeat/worker results.
- Native desktop and relevant Web walkthrough evidence.
- Known limitations and explicit gaps.
- G-V presentation recommendation plus a separate **H-ready** note stating which candidate dimensions/scenarios are now safe to submit to human evaluation.

## Decision unlocked

Completion may unlock two independent next steps:

1. **G-V:** retain current presentation or admit a separately scoped render migration based on V evidence.
2. **H admission:** authorize a later human-led material-feel study using the verified lab to classify Water semantic candidates as preferred / acceptable / unacceptable and to identify named perceptual deficits that may justify #18.

#19 does **not** choose Water's production mass bits, coherent duration, Cell packing, spare-bit use or compact motion semantics.

The intended workflow after this revision is:

```text
#17 quantitative precision evidence
        ↓
#19 V1 presentation + V2 Water Feel Lab/runtime policies
        ↓
verified H-ready apparatus
        ↓
separate human material-feel evaluation
        ↓
perceptually acceptable state budgets + named deficits
        ↓
#18 only where an admitted motion/history question remains
```

## Repository / execution context

Work from the verified current local CyberSand source, not an older remote control. Read the repository/workspace AGENTS instructions and the required focused documentation before changes. Preserve the intentionally dirty Windows DLL and unrelated work. Keep builds/toolchains/raw validation outside committed source according to existing repository policy.

Read and reuse, without rewriting their conclusions:

- completed #15 liquid characterization;
- completed #16 layout/packing evidence;
- completed #17 state-precision evidence and its registered quantization rules;
- completed #13 Experiment Tower/tuning-profile design and retained implementation evidence;
- current Water/material/render contracts;
- ADR-003 immutable handoff, ADR-005 Water model, ADR-008 bounded approximation, ADR-010 failure quarantine and ADR-011 granular policy.

The existing local prompt path `docs/operations/architecture-programme-prompts/fractional-presentation.md` and master `docs/operations/architecture-programme.md` must be synchronized to this revised issue scope during implementation/documentation work. Until then, this GitHub issue is the current revised execution contract for #19.

# Architecture experiment: gate and test bounded sparse ballistic material transfer

## Identity and dependencies

Issue: [#20](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/20).
Programme/workstream: B; master programme (`../architecture-programme.md` in the local planning checkout).
Dependencies: Implementation blocked by C/L/P/M evidence and G-B admission. Design/admission can inspect I's recovered proposal and existing #12. Do not require arbitrary generated bodies; use current rectangle values only.

GitHub completion dependencies: [#18](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/18)
Staged gate decisions and the complete master mirror: [#14](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/14). A gate entry may be recorded before #14 closes; its final-completion dependency is not a circular prerequisite.

This prompt is executable without the four original conversations.

## Objective

Produce either a justified no-go or one bounded proof that sparse event-driven motion plus safe reinsertion solves a named unmet high-speed requirement.

## Why this work exists

I recommended ballistic material before coherent detachment because continuous travel need not enlarge cellular worker writes. Later Water/Bytes evidence may meet the actual need more cheaply; that must be tested first.

## Relevant Current architecture and accepted decisions

Work in C:/kybersand/source; read C:/kybersand/AGENTS.md and source AGENTS.md and their required focused docs before changes. Use the pinned workspace toolchain and a separate codex/ experiment branch. Preserve the deliberately dirty Windows DLL, any user-loaded runtime and unrelated changes. Keep toolchains/builds/raw logs under C:/kybersand, not C:/cybersand. Programme intake is 8f4ffb96e03dc50cb43ab9c84de17ccb44c03774; remote main was ab4851e and lacked local #9/#10/#13/Water changes. Obtain the named source checkpoint from the active local repository and inspect actual HEAD/deltas rather than running an older remote as the control.

CURRENT: native cells are material 8/state_a 8/state_b 8/epoch 8; no generic vx/vy. Water alone uses fractional FreeMass, mass1..255 (Empty zero), state_b coherent-emission countdown 12, merge=max, pre-decrement suppression; film 48/255; current floor(3*imbalance/4) lateral relaxation and tolerance1. Other liquids generally move whole cells; Oil is specialized. Temperature is persistent optional chunk state. CURRENT POLICY: powder/powder density exchange excluded; Mercury period 30; sampled player support separate; #13 mixing/carrying opt-in, protected horizontal 2/cadence 1. Changing actual Water flux can change opt-in pickup even with the same profile hash.

ACCEPTED: ADR-001 native material authority; ADR-002 phased exclusive write domains; ADR-003 immutable snapshots; ADR-004 paused excluded regions/no catch-up; ADR-005 exact closed Water mass and stable equilibrium; ADR-007 independent main-thread Rapier body state and separate transient occupancy; ADR-008 explicit bounded approximation; ADR-009 pinned Rapier; ADR-010 quarantine failed ticks; ADR-011 versioned granular policy. Do not silently invalidate these. In particular no occupancy in persistent Cell, worker Godot/Rapier calls, silent material deletion, mutable snapshot views or global rollback claims. A discussion of relaxed numerical conservation is an OPEN proposal, not an amended ADR. #13's no-velocity restriction was ISSUE-SCOPED; this prompt's non-goals likewise do not create permanent policy.

Geometry is independently 128x128 storage,32x32 activity,64x64 scheduling core, maximum write radius2 (68x68 expanded domain). Native liquid operations are local; do not copy fallback long-range Water. Desktop pacing is asynchronous against main-thread Rapier; native Web waits synchronously, with optional internal workers. Fallback and serial have different semantics. Current rectangles lack general pixel membership. #11 is administratively closed but the intake source/evidence still documents missing bearing and barrier-aware ejection; preserve that unresolved distinction.

## Hypothesis / question

Does a sparse promoted representation justify its ownership, sweep, lifecycle and memory cost versus local history/current transport for a defined event?

## Scope

Admission and reviewed transfer charter first. If admitted, one nonreactive material, one bounded event emitter, a fixed native pool, continuous/fixed-point positions and velocities, swept grid/barrier/rectangle-mask collision, and bounded near-rest reinsertion. Preserve material/state and temperature where applicable; add Water only as a separately admitted fractional-ledger case.

## Non-goals

No production ballistic migration, unlimited particle objects, automatic fallback for every overlap, arbitrary coherent bodies, registry expansion, full DamageEvent/destruction framework, general reactions, fracture, torque or new physics backend.

## Repository touchpoints

`native/include/cybersand/world.hpp`, `native/src/world.cpp`: serialized explosion/event boundary, cell transfer, activity and failed state; `native/include/cybersand/physics_diagnostics.hpp`, `c_api.h`; `godot/native_extension/cyber_native_cell_world.cpp`: prepare_rigid_body_coupling / rasterization/reconciliation; `godot/scripts/rapier_physics_bridge.gd`; `native/bench/physics_characterisation.cpp`, `godot/tests/test_physics_characterisation.gd`, `tools/physics/water-accounting.json`. Any new ballistic module is proposed, not an existing file.
These are inspected existing files/symbols; proposed new modules must be named as new.

## Experimental or implementation strategy

1. At G-B register the event, why local M/current motion cannot satisfy it, measurable target and bounded costs. Without that evidence close no-go successfully. Do not claim I's recommendation is authorization for an unconditional production system.
2. Review a singular-owner contract: cells own before promotion; reserved slots own nothing; after revision/capacity checks at exclusive boundary commit extraction and transfer authority to pool. Failed admission leaves cell intact. During flight pool owns payload; reinsertion reserves a legal destination and commits once. Failed placement retains particle/pending owner and reports deferral, never expires material away.
3. Start with research budgets of 256 pool slots, 64 promotion attempts/tick,64 grid crossings/particle/tick and 8-cell reinsertion search; register exact deterministic behavior when a budget is hit. These are experiment limits, not accepted production constants. No unbounded per-tick allocation or global sparse-world scan.
4. Use event-provided motion with declared units (cell pixels/s, fixed 60Hz step) and deterministic slot/event ordering. Swept collision must check intervening hard cells; reaching traversal budget defers travel, not skips barriers. Reuse immutable rectangle occupancy; central reaction impulses may remain disabled and must be labeled.
5. Test saturation, stale source revision, cancel, reinsertion full, region exit, failure quarantine and repeated promote/demote. Keep compact material payload/temperature and quantity ledger exact; motion rounding/loss is a separate account.
6. Compare matched controls and sparse/dense event load. Do not turn all no-destination cases into silent deletion or unlimited particles. Report continue/no-go with cost and uncovered production cases.

## Controlled variables

Changes: Explicit sparse representation/motion and transfer semantics; comparison is a feature experiment, not raw Cell-width measurement.

Fixed: Current underlying Cell/layout control, liquid/powder policies, scheduler geometry, main-thread Rapier, source event inputs, bounded occupancy and no full-world scan. No semantic changes to cells not promoted.

## Instrumentation

Ownership census before/after every transfer, material/state/temperature/quantity totals, pending/refused counts and reasons; event/handle determinism; trajectory/range/swept barrier results; motion quantization; pool/queue/scratch high-water, work per tick, allocations and p50/p95/p99/max/total cost. Include baseline plus whole-system promotion/lookup/render costs.

Register primary metrics, targets, run budget, capacities and rejection criteria before candidate code. Default behavior screen: five seeds/translations, 1/4 workers, 1800 ticks. Epoch work needs at least 2048 ticks. Use 7 interleaved baseline/candidate process pairs for timing, declared 120-tick steady warmup, and separate initial-settling/startup measurements. Avoid overlapping builds. Register any smaller/larger necessary sample before results; retain failures/outliers. Flag >15% paired p95 cost regression or >1ms extra epoch-clear excess for review; these are research screens, not accepted production limits. Missing counters/hardware produce explicit gaps. No requirement to rerun historical campaigns.

## Fixtures / benchmark scenarios

One event ejects selected nonreactive grains horizontally/diagonally into hard thin barriers and the current rectangle mask; low/high load and pool saturation, near-rest return, entirely full return region, negative/core/chunk seams and offscreen pause/re-entry.
